title: Documents panel offers Start reviewing only where the document machine allows start_review
rootCause:
The finding has two halves. The first is already fixed on main; the second is still live. Main is now 117717c, a QA/docs-only commit on top of b59bbf0. No frontend or backend file changed, so every citation below holds.

(a) The unhandled error and the frozen page (fixed by DOS-029: d600ab8, merged in d8ae49e with the DOS-135 repair 8161f21):
- In the Phase 1 build, Start reviewing ran `void startReview.mutateAsync(selected ?? '').then((result) => { setSessionId(result.session.id) })` with no rejection handler.
- `useMutation.mutateAsync` rethrows the ApiError on purpose (frontend/libs/api-client/src/react/index.tsx:396-401). The 409 therefore became an unhandled rejection, and Expo's dev overlay took over the page.
- DOS-029 added `stayOpen` as the rejection handler (frontend/manager-app/app/inbound/documents.tsx:486-488; helper frontend/manager-app/src/lib/ui.tsx:232) and the panel `<Refusal>` (documents.tsx:475-479).
- All 53 `mutateAsync` call sites in frontend/manager-app/app now have a rejection handler (git grep, each checked).
- QA/14-regression-results.md:156 (DOS-029e control) shows Start reviewing's 409 as a sentence above the button, with no overlay. DOS-135 (QA/14:162) keeps that sentence visible when a sibling write is pending.
- The finding's "catch ApiError in the mutation hook" is wrong. `mutate()` already swallows errors (index.tsx:406-413). `mutateAsync` must reject so that `.then(done, stayOpen)` keeps a refused dialog open.

(b) The button that can never work (still live):
- documents.tsx:480-491 renders Start reviewing whenever `mayReview` (a permission, l.101) is true and `sessionId` (local state, l.104) is null. It never reads `doc.status` (DocumentSchema.status, backend/libs/contracts/src/docint.ts:314).
- The server takes the lock only from `extracted` or `needs_review` and answers 409 otherwise (backend/libs/core/src/modules/docint/review.service.ts:91-94). It then fires `start_review` through the machine (l.148).
- Those are exactly the two states with a `start_review` transition in documentMachine (backend/libs/domain/src/state-machines/document.ts:57 and :64). `reviewed` has only commit, retry and reject (l.72). committed, rejected and failed are terminal (l.46, l.73-75).
- The worklist includes `reviewed` and `failed` (QueueStatusSchema, contracts docint.ts:259-264; queue.service.ts:30 and :51). Every Reviewed or Failed row therefore opens a panel whose Start reviewing the server always refuses.
- Selecting a row resets `sessionId` to null (documents.tsx:313-318), so a Reviewed document opened from the register always shows Start reviewing. That is the finding's path: in QA/evidence/phase1/manager/32-document-gur.txt, GUR/26-27/00490 was already Reviewed (29 h old) when opened.
- No second cause. The server's guard is right. No trigger or RLS policy is involved. The manager desk has no offline or sync path for docint. No other app calls review.start (git grep over frontend).

Data on dos_qa (read-only SQL, 2026-09-13):
- Documents by status: uploaded 7, extracted 2, needs_review 5, committed 2, failed 1. There is no reviewed row.
- GUR/26-27/00490 (76f4437a-df67-755e-acf9-1a7486050bc4) is committed with a submitted session, so it is out of the worklist.
- The live repro is the Failed MOM Foods — Bikaner document 9de6b4c7-4144-7d22-9daa-dd6a53b5c631, which has 0 extractions. Its `reading` query is disabled and starts `idle` (frontend/libs/api-client/src/cache.ts:36), so `isLoading` is false (react/index.tsx:286). `<Async>` (ui.tsx:185) therefore renders the panel with its Start reviewing button.

changes.what:
Written first, as one describe('DOS-031 …') with three cases.
(1) 'reviewed' and 'failed' → false.
(2) An exhaustive literal table `{ uploaded: false, verifying: false, extracting: false, extracted: true, needs_review: true, reviewed: false, committed: false, rejected: false, failed: false } satisfies Record<DocumentStatus, boolean>`, each row asserted with the status as the message. The table is the server's list at review.service.ts:91. `satisfies` makes `pnpm typecheck` fail if the contract gains a status without a row (the manager-app tsconfig includes src).
(3) A screen guard that reads app/inbound/documents.tsx as text, following frontend/sales-app/src/order-entry-layout.test.ts:
- `node:fs` and `node:url` come in through non-literal specifiers, because env.d.ts keeps @types/node out of an app.
- The path is `fileURLToPath(new URL('../../app/inbound/documents.tsx', import.meta.url))` (the path has a space), with comments stripped.
- It asserts that the file imports `mayStartReview` from '../../src/lib/review-desk'.
- It asserts that a `mayStartReview(doc.status)` exists before `testID="docint-start"`, and that exactly one `<Button` lies between the last such occurrence and that testID, so the gate wraps the Start button itself.
Imports: `import type { DocumentStatus } from '@dos/contracts'`, `mayStartReview` from './review-desk', and vitest.
Red phase: add review-desk.ts as a stub `export function mayStartReview(_status: DocumentStatus): boolean { return true }` (today's behaviour) and leave documents.tsx untouched. All three cases then fail on assertions, not on a missing module. Then implement.

`export function mayStartReview(status: DocumentStatus): boolean { return documentMachine.can(status, 'start_review') }`, with `import type { DocumentStatus } from '@dos/contracts'` and `import { documentMachine } from '@dos/domain'`.
- The manager app already depends on @dos/domain (package.json; documents.tsx:23).
- The precedent for a machine's `can()` deciding a control on the device is frontend/delivery-app/src/lib/trip-choice.ts:9 and :62 (`tripMachine.can`).
- Doc comment: this is the transition table the server's `transition(tx, doc, 'start_review')` applies (review.service.ts:148), equal today to the guard at review.service.ts:91-94. Start reviewing is offered only on such a document.

tests.name: DOS-031: Start reviewing is not offered on a reviewed or failed document (the two worklist states review.start refuses)
DOS-031: Start reviewing is offered on exactly the statuses review.start accepts (extracted, needs_review), for every DocumentStatus
DOS-031: documents.tsx renders the docint-start button only inside a mayStartReview(doc.status) branch

A. Failed document (no write):

The transaction rolls back and nothing is written.

B. Reviewed document (two writes, so lane DB only, never dos_qa):
- Prepare once: open GUR/26-27/00496 (9d12c063-388e-72d8-94d0-88d0abef7aa5, Extracted; all 12 checks pass on dos_qa). Press Start reviewing (200), then This reading is right → confirm (200). The chip reads Reviewed.

risk:
Low. The change is frontend-only: one screen, one branch. There is no contract, permission, schema, backend or kit change, and the server's 409 at review.service.ts:91-94 stays as the backstop. The rule reads the same transition table the server's transition() applies, and the exhaustive typed table pins it to the server's list.
Residuals:
- If another desk moves a document between refetches, the cached status can still offer Start once. The 409 and DOS-029's Refusal cover that, with no overlay.
- The in-session controls after a successful submit in the same panel are deliberately unchanged (notes R1). They are refused with a sentence, as today.
- The screen guard reads source text, so a harmless refactor of that ternary (renaming `doc`, say) fails it. That is the known cost of the order-entry-layout.test.ts pattern.
reviewNotes:
WHAT I CHANGED
1. Narrowed the scope to Start reviewing, which is what the finding and its suggested fix cover.
- The plan wrapped the in-session trio (Save / This reading is right / Give it up) in the same gate. That creates a new silent state. After a successful submit, `sessionId` stays set, so Bill no. (documents.tsx:413) and Amount (l.420) stay editable while Save disappears. Whatever is typed goes nowhere, with no refusal.
- It also changes the submit path, which the finding never walked (charter: nothing adjacent).
- The trio-after-submit defect is recorded as R1 in notes, with the right fix shape: clear the session on submit success, as Give it up does at l.518-520. The plan's own reviewNotes offered this narrowing.
2. Added a third test: a screen guard that reads documents.tsx as text (the frontend/sales-app/src/order-entry-layout.test.ts pattern, also asked for in the DOS-146 review). The screen cannot be imported under vitest, so without the guard the helper spec stays green even if the screen never calls the helper.
3. Red phase: the stub now also leaves documents.tsx untouched, so all three cases fail on assertions.
4. Corrected verification B. In the same page, after start → submit, pressing Start reviewing does not get the finding's 409. The hook keeps the same meta for the same document id (api-client react/index.tsx:380-386), and the server replays the stored 200 of the first start (backend/libs/core/src/platform/idempotency.ts:61-74), so the panel shows the old session. B now reloads the page first. It also says the trio stays after the submit on both builds, so a verifier does not read that as a failed fix.
5. Devices and environment:
- Added an iOS step (ios-drive.mjs `has`), limited to A. B's confirm Dialog opens inside a Sheet, which never presents on iOS (DOS-164).
- The Android dump is taken before any press and matches text or content-desc (DOS-158).
- The environment section now says the Metros are stopped (QA/STATE.md) and that a Metro under CI=1 never reloads.
6. Corrected citations and one overclaim:
- document.ts: terminal l.46, start_review l.57 and l.64, reviewed l.72, failed l.75.
- heldSession refusal: review.service.ts:348-351. mutateAsync rethrow: react/index.tsx:396-401.
- DOS-029 is d600ab8, merged in d8ae49e with DOS-135's 8161f21.
- The plan said the typed table 'fails the test if either side drifts'. It pins the client to the domain machine and to a literal copy of the server's list, but no backend spec pins the hand-written guard at review.service.ts:91-94: docint.spec.ts has no start-refusal case.
- The closer precedent for a machine deciding a control on the device is delivery-app/src/lib/trip-choice.ts:9 and :62 (`tripMachine.can`), not api-client or ui.

KEPT (verified)
- Root cause (a): all 53 mutateAsync call sites in manager-app/app have a rejection handler, `mutate` swallows errors (index.tsx:406-413), and the finding's 'catch ApiError in the hook' would bring back DOS-029.
- Root cause (b): the Start branch never reads doc.status. The server guard, the machine and the worklist statuses are as cited.
- The helper built on documentMachine.can, the exhaustive `satisfies Record<DocumentStatus, boolean>` table (the manager-app tsconfig includes src, so typecheck enforces it), placement under src/lib, and the load-out.test.ts style.
- No contract, permission, schema, backend or kit change; size S; dependsOn [].
- dos_qa data: the status counts and ids; 12 of 12 checks passed on 9d12c063 and on 5929e4e4; 0 extractions on 9de6b4c7; an open session on 2254e884; 76f4437a committed with a submitted session.

COULD NOT CONFIRM (read-only review)
- Any browser or device behaviour: the Metros are stopped and no walk was run.
- The lane DB's rows. It is a copy of dos_test_batch2_template, built from b59bbf0, and its ids or statuses may differ from dos_qa.
- R2 (the Start replay after Give it up) comes from reading idempotency.ts and useMutation, not from a walk.
- Whether XCUITest's page source includes the panel's off-screen buttons; the iOS step swipes if not.

RESIDUAL DOUBTS
- A Fable sign-off may prefer the wider gate. If so, it must also clear sessionId and the header edits on submit success, or the header inputs stay editable with no Save.
- The cached status can still offer Start once if another desk moves the document between refetches. The server's 409 and the Refusal cover it, with no overlay.
- The screen guard is source-text based and fails on a harmless rename of `doc` in that branch. That is the accepted cost of the pattern.

Save / This reading is right / Give it up and the editable Bill no. and Amount (l.413, l.420) therefore stay on a Reviewed document, and each write is refused "review session … is submitted" (review.service.ts:348-351). Fix shape: clear sessionId and the header edits on submit success, as Give it up does (l.518-520).

The server replays the first start's stored 200 (idempotency.ts:61-74), so the panel shows an abandoned session and every in-session write is refused. Fix shape: `startReview.reset()` once the session ends.
  - R3: Reject the document on a Failed document always gets 409 (`document: cannot apply "reject" in state "failed"`). documents.service.ts:509 applies the machine, and failed is terminal (document.ts:75).

  - DOS-037 (P1) may narrow the accountant's docint permissions. The gate sits inside the `mayReview` branch (l.473), so the two compose.
  - DOS-030 (P2) edits the Book it button in the same block (l.537-548): textual only.
  - DOS-141 (P3) may reword the 409 sentences used in verify A, B and C; match substrings.
  - DOS-158 (P3): Android content-desc 'busy' after a press; the dump is taken before any press.
  - Held plans (DOS-032+059, 074+097, 096, 003, 004, 106, 043, 007, 056/156): none touches docint or documents.tsx (grep of QA/evidence/batch1/held-review-brief.md).
  - Batch-2 plans on disk (DOS-115, 132, 133, 146) do not edit documents.tsx. DOS-146 only names documents.tsx:418 as a same-class RupeeInput case it does not fix. There is no lanes.md or inventory.md yet to check lane placement.
- docs/22 has no review-desk rule to update (a grep for review lock / Start reviewing / review desk finds nothing), and no product decision is involved.
- Suggested commit message: `fix(DOS-031): the documents panel offers Start reviewing only where the document machine allows start_review`, with a Test: line naming review-desk.test.ts › DOS-031.
